hints.content:
We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C+D)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C+\blueD A\cdot D$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of p squared and a length of negative p squared. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is negative p and the length is negative p squared. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative one with a length of negative p squared.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{-p^2}(p^2-p-1)
\\\\
&=\goldE{-p^2}(p^2)+(\goldE{-p^2})(-p)+(\goldE{-p^2})(-1)
\\\\
&=-p^4+p^3+p^2
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of p squared and a length of negative p squared. Inside of this rectangle is negative p to the fourth power. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is negative p and the length is negative p squared. Inside of this rectangle is p cubed. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative one with a length of negative p squared. Inside of this rectangle is p squared.

question.content:
